Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@mediplan.com>
Date: 2028-11-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Activation windows & SLA exceptions for private offer - Mediplan

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is aligned on Redwood for our inference baseline. Legal and procurement are working through the standard AWS private offer flow, but we have two time-sensitive asks before we can final sign-off: 

1) Activation window: Our security team requires activation (PO acceptance + account activation) within a 10-business-day window from signature to start ingesting production data. Is that something Redwood can commit to on this private offer?

2) SLA exception: We have an internal requirement to include a 99.9% monthly uptime commitment for the inference endpoint and would like to understand if Redwood can support an SLA exception for the private-offer buyer (or provide a documented fallback plan that preserves availability during incidents).

Can you confirm whether these two items are negotiable and what evidence / intake you need from us (CISO contact, environment details, expected RPS, etc.)? We hope to close by the end of this month.

Appreciate it —
Laura
Procurement Manager, Mediplan

--
Mediplan Inc.

Subject: Re: Activation windows & SLA exceptions for private offer - Mediplan

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front: we can usually commit to a 10-business-day activation window for private offers if procurement + legal signatures are received and we have the required evidence pack; SLA exceptions are possible on a case-by-case basis — they require an internal review (security + infra) and a delegated exec approval for changes to standard terms.

What we need from Mediplan to accelerate:
- CISO contact and SOC2 point-of-contact (for evidence review)
- Expected steady-state RPS and peak concurrency (example: 50 RPS steady, 200 peak)
- A short list of required uptime & remediation expectations (you mentioned 99.9% — is that for the inference endpoint only or for control-plane availability too?)

Vanessa / Jordan — can you confirm the internal approval path for SLA exceptions and whether we have a templated fallback addendum for private offers? If this needs an exec exception, flag the expected delta in financial / operational risk so I can route to the approvals committee.

I can pull our activation checklist and an example evidence pack; I’ll attach those once Vanessa confirms the approval route.

Best,
Irene
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Activation windows & SLA exceptions for private offer - Mediplan

Forwarding Laura's note — Mediplan needs a 10-business-day activation window and is asking for a 99.9% SLA for the inference endpoint.

Internal ask: what is the quickest approval cadence for an SLA exception? I want to keep this a low-friction enterprise close (Mediplan is already leaning on Redwood), but we should quantify the operational cost if we accept 99.9% vs our standard 99.5%.

Jordan — can you prepare a concise risk/impact blurb (3 bullets max) that I can include in the approvals ticket? Vanessa — do we have a standard fallback addendum (e.g., multi-region failover + reduced credits during incidents) we can offer instead of an SLA tweak?

Proposed timeline: collect evidence (2 business days), approvals review (3 business days), activation scheduling (up to 5 business days) — total fits within their 10-business-day ask if approvals are fast. Note: if approvals take longer we can propose a phased activation (start with staging access + ingest for non-PII workloads).

Thanks —
Irene
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Hi Laura —

Appreciate the timeline. We can meet the 10-business-day activation window provided: 1) signed private-offer in AWS PO console, 2) submission of the evidence pack (SOC2 report + CISO contact), and 3) confirmation of the expected RPS/peak concurrency. I’ve attached the activation checklist and an evidence example to this thread.

Regarding the 99.9% request: our standard buyer-facing SLA for private offers is 99.5% for inference endpoints. We can offer a 99.9% commitment via an SLA exception subject to: 
- a short operational addendum (multi-region failover + a documented runbook), and
- a one-time remediation credit cap that aligns with the increased SLO (we typically set this as a percent of monthly invoice).

To keep this moving quickly, here’s what I’m proposing:
1) Mediplan submits the SOC2 evidence and RPS numbers by EOD Tuesday (2028-11-14).
2) Redwood prepares an operational addendum and exception request; we’ll route to our approvals committee and confirm cost delta within 48 hours.
3) Once approved, we generate the DocuSign for the addendum and activate the private offer in AWS (target within 7 business days of DocuSign completion).

I’m including a DocuSign link for the addendum and the AWS PO activation checklist below. If you prefer, we can do a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through items and speed approvals.
